Owner: captain for integration/workflows, native performance lane for fixture diagnostics, independent semantic/evidence reviewer. Baseline: publication `732d9cc`, with both original failed macOS logs retained; local implementation `896d851` remains separately qualified. Allowed work is finite exact-source normal/race profiling, a build-tag-only numeric fixture seam with no new wire authority, and a separate macOS 26/Ubuntu 24.04 diagnostic workflow. Preserve the original 2MiB/eight-second/Unicode/CPR/child-survival predicates. Later diagnostic completion cannot erase an original gate failure. Runtime correction requires a measured bottleneck, independent semantic review and fresh exact local/hosted qualification. No provider/model/customer/production work is part of this lane. Public v0.2.1 remains the installer target.

Local integration `d0d882d` passed full normal/race source checks, vet and twelve documentation tests. Publication `5abdf0b` preserves all 430 Go file objects/modes and passed all six hosted Source and packaging jobs. Its separate investigation passed every original/tagged native gate, but Ubuntu's normal allocation-summary sanitization failed after successful `pprof`; the exact rejection is unknown and retained. The bounded numeric phase/reason driver repair and its administrative observer passed independent offline review, including refusal of contradictory codes. Next: publish one fresh source and observe both workflows. Preserve strict rejection, generic failure labels, raw-data privacy, all Go/workflow bytes and modes, and the original baseline/deadlines. No old-head rerun or runtime optimization is included. Sampled screen profiles do not establish the historical failing pipeline's cause.

The five lanes roll through the finite worker pool. Provider/tool declarations are model-neutral; each native mapping reports supported, applied and unknown fields separately. Native model turns and customer message destinations retain their existing independent authorization and qualification gates.

The current controls increment provides a saved-profile picker, direct per-tool switches with preserved pins and independent profiles, and explicit requested-model projection for reviewed Gemini/Grok/OpenCode versions. Retrying only an operation ID uses its original profile snapshot, argv and home lifetime; it cannot create a missing intent or select a newer profile. Gemini's native MCP server selector is refused when it would override an applied profile. Source and terminal-control qualification do not imply native provider loading or accepted model routing.
